edits.old:
We see that the extra return per unit of volatility risk
$d Z _ { 2 }$ is given by $\phi ( S , \nu , t ) d t$ and so in analogy with
the Capital Asset Pricing Model, $\phi$ is known as the market price of
volatility risk.\footnote{\textbf{Editorial note:} combining the valuation
equation (1.3) with the SDE (1.2) as printed (diffusion
$\eta \beta \sqrt { \nu } d Z _ { 2 }$) gives a noise term
$\eta \beta \sqrt { \nu } \frac { \partial V } { \partial \nu } d Z _ { 2 }$,
whereas the final line of the display above reads
$\beta \sqrt { \nu } \frac { \partial V } { \partial \nu } d Z _ { 2 }$.
The printed reading is internally consistent with the risk-neutral SDE
$d \nu = \alpha ' d t + \beta \sqrt { \nu } d Z _ { 2 }$ printed below if
volatility risk is measured per unit of $\beta \sqrt { \nu } d Z _ { 2 }$
(i.e., $d Z _ { 2 }$ rescaled by $\eta$, or $\eta = 1$, from this point on);
taken literally with (1.2), the factor $\eta$ is missing. Preserved as
printed; both extractions agree on the absence of $\eta$, so inspection of
printed p.~7 would be confirmatory only.}
